_about: Hand-written key points for pyt-biochemistry.html (27 Nov 2026, lead). Samples: FMGE recalls, no images.
subject: Biochemistry
intro: Biochemistry in FMGE comes down to rate-limiting enzymes, vitamin deficiencies, inborn errors and a few lab markers. These are the topics that keep coming back, most-asked first, with the one thing to remember about each.

bc.iem.title: Inborn errors of metabolism (overview)
bc.iem.note: Most are autosomal recessive. Clues: a sick newborn after feeds starting, unusual urine smell, hypoglycaemia, acidosis or high ammonia. Galactosaemia (cataract, E. coli sepsis), PKU (musty odour), MSUD (maple syrup urine), urea cycle defects (high ammonia, no acidosis), Von Gierke (hypoglycaemia, lactic acidosis).
bc.iem.why: Fasting hypoglycaemia, lactic acidosis, high uric acid and a big liver point to glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency (Von Gierke).

bc.aa.dis.note: PKU: phenylalanine hydroxylase, musty odour, fair skin. Alkaptonuria: homogentisate oxidase, urine darkens on standing, blue-black ear cartilage (ochronosis), arthritis. MSUD: branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase. Homocystinuria: cystathionine β-synthase, downward lens dislocation, clots. Albinism: tyrosinase.
bc.aa.dis.why: Dark urine with blue-black ear cartilage is alkaptonuria, from homogentisate oxidase deficiency.

bc.vit.title: Vitamins and cofactors
bc.vit.note: B1 thiamine (pyruvate dehydrogenase, transketolase): beriberi, Wernicke. B2: cheilosis. B3 niacin: pellagra (dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia), also in Hartnup and carcinoid. B6: neuropathy with isoniazid, sideroblastic anaemia. B12 and folate: megaloblastic anaemia. Vitamin C (with copper) is needed for collagen cross-linking: scurvy.
bc.vit.why: Collagen needs vitamin C for hydroxylation and copper (lysyl oxidase) for cross-linking.

bc.carb.glyco.note: Glycogen storage diseases: type I Von Gierke (glucose-6-phosphatase): fasting hypoglycaemia, lactic acidosis, high uric acid and lipids, big liver. II Pompe (acid maltase, lysosomal): heart failure in infants. III Cori (debranching). V McArdle (muscle phosphorylase): cramps on exercise, no lactate rise. Glycogen synthase and phosphorylase are the key enzymes.

bc.mol.dna.note: DNA polymerase III makes most new DNA in bacteria; telomerase keeps chromosome ends. Repair: nucleotide excision (thymine dimers from UV; xeroderma pigmentosum), base excision, mismatch repair (Lynch syndrome), homologous recombination (BRCA).
bc.mol.dna.why: Thymine dimers from UV light are removed by nucleotide excision repair.

bc.mol.gen.note: Autosomal dominant: often structural (Marfan, ADPKD, Huntington, NF). Autosomal recessive: mostly enzyme defects. X-linked recessive: haemophilia, Duchenne (dystrophin, the largest gene), G6PD, colour blindness. Mitochondrial: from the mother only. Imprinting: Prader-Willi (paternal 15q loss), Angelman (maternal).
bc.mol.gen.why: Duchenne muscular dystrophy is caused by mutations in the dystrophin gene.

bc.mol.rna.note: RNA polymerase I: rRNA; II: mRNA (blocked by α-amanitin); III: tRNA and 5S rRNA. mRNA processing: 5′ cap, poly-A tail, splicing of introns (snRNPs; anti-Smith antibodies target them).
bc.mol.rna.why: RNA polymerase II makes messenger RNA in eukaryotes.

bc.mol.prot.note: Translation starts at AUG (methionine); stop codons UAA, UAG, UGA. The genetic code is degenerate and universal. Post-translational changes: hydroxylation (collagen, needs vitamin C), glycosylation, phosphorylation, gamma-carboxylation (vitamin K), subunit assembly. Proteins are tagged for breakdown with ubiquitin.

bc.mol.dis.note: Trinucleotide repeats: Fragile X (CGG; long face, big ears, large testes), Huntington (CAG), myotonic dystrophy (CTG), Friedreich ataxia (GAA). Anticipation: worse and earlier in later generations. Cystic fibrosis: CFTR chloride channel (ΔF508 the commonest).
bc.mol.dis.why: The CFTR protein is a chloride channel; its defect blocks chloride transport.

bc.lip.fa.note: Carnitine carries long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria (carnitine palmitoyltransferase I, blocked by malonyl-CoA). β-oxidation gives acetyl-CoA. Fatty acid synthesis: acetyl-CoA carboxylase is rate-limiting (needs biotin). Ketone bodies (acetoacetate, β-hydroxybutyrate) are made in the liver but the liver cannot use them.
bc.lip.fa.why: Carnitine shuttles long-chain fatty acids across the inner mitochondrial membrane.

bc.lip.lp.note: Chylomicrons: dietary fat (apoB-48). VLDL: liver-made triglyceride. LDL: carries cholesterol to tissues (apoB-100); familial hypercholesterolaemia is an LDL receptor defect. HDL: reverse cholesterol transport (apoA-I). Lipoprotein lipase needs apoC-II.
bc.lip.lp.why: HDL carries cholesterol from tissues back to the liver: reverse cholesterol transport.

bc.lip.chol.note: HMG-CoA reductase is the rate-limiting enzyme of cholesterol synthesis (statins block it). Cholesterol makes bile acids, steroid hormones and vitamin D. HDL takes cholesterol back to the liver.

bc.carb.glyc.note: Phosphofructokinase-1 is rate-limiting, activated by fructose-2,6-bisphosphate and AMP, inhibited by ATP and citrate. Net gain: 2 ATP per glucose in anaerobic glycolysis. Red cells depend fully on glycolysis; pyruvate kinase deficiency causes haemolysis.
bc.carb.glyc.why: PFK-1 is the rate-limiting enzyme of glycolysis and is activated by fructose-2,6-bisphosphate.

bc.carb.tca.note: Takes place in the mitochondrial matrix. Isocitrate dehydrogenase is the rate-limiting enzyme. One turn gives 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, 1 GTP. Pyruvate dehydrogenase links glycolysis to the cycle (needs B1, B2, B3, B5 and lipoic acid; arsenic blocks it).

bc.carb.gng.note: Makes glucose from lactate, glycerol and amino acids, mainly in the liver (and kidney in starvation). Key enzymes: pyruvate carboxylase (activated by acetyl-CoA, needs biotin), PEPCK, fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase, glucose-6-phosphatase. Muscle lacks glucose-6-phosphatase.
bc.carb.gng.why: Acetyl-CoA activates pyruvate carboxylase, pushing pyruvate towards glucose.

bc.carb.hmp.note: The pentose phosphate pathway makes NADPH (for fat synthesis and to keep glutathione reduced) and ribose-5-phosphate (for nucleotides). G6PD is the rate-limiting enzyme; its deficiency leaves red cells open to oxidant damage (Heinz bodies, bite cells). Transketolase needs thiamine.
bc.carb.hmp.why: The pentose phosphate pathway produces NADPH and ribose-5-phosphate, not ATP.

bc.aa.urea.note: Happens in the liver, partly in mitochondria. Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I is rate-limiting, activated by N-acetylglutamate. Ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency (X-linked) is the commonest urea cycle defect: high ammonia and orotic acid. High ammonia without acidosis suggests a urea cycle defect.
bc.aa.urea.why: N-acetylglutamate is the essential allosteric activator of carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I.

bc.aa.nt.note: Tyrosine: dopamine, noradrenaline, adrenaline, thyroxine, melanin. Tryptophan: serotonin, melatonin, niacin. Histidine: histamine. Glutamate: GABA. Arginine: nitric oxide (NO synthase). Glycine: haem, creatine and glutathione are built partly from it.
bc.aa.nt.why: Nitric oxide is made from arginine by nitric oxide synthase.

bc.enz.kin.note: Km = substrate concentration at half Vmax (low Km = high affinity). Turnover number (kcat): molecules converted per enzyme per unit time. Competitive inhibitor: Km up, Vmax same. Non-competitive: Vmax down, Km same. Lineweaver-Burk plot shows the difference.
bc.enz.kin.why: Molecules converted per minute by a fully saturated enzyme is the turnover number (kcat).

bc.enz.clin.note: ALT: the most specific for liver cell injury. ALP and GGT: cholestasis (ALP also bone). Amylase and lipase: pancreatitis (lipase more specific, stays up longer). Troponin: heart. CK-MB rises again with re-infarction. LDH rises in haemolysis and lymphoma.
bc.enz.clin.why: Amylase (and lipase) rise in acute pancreatitis.

bc.cell.org.note: Peroxisomes: very long chain fatty acid breakdown (Zellweger syndrome, adrenoleukodystrophy). Lysosomes: storage diseases (Tay-Sachs, Gaucher, Niemann-Pick, Pompe); I-cell disease is a failure to tag enzymes with mannose-6-phosphate. Mitochondria: energy, inherited from the mother.
bc.cell.org.why: Zellweger syndrome is a failure to form peroxisomes.

bc.cell.cyto.note: Microtubules (tubulin): kinesin moves cargo outward (anterograde), dynein moves it back towards the cell body (retrograde; rabies and polio travel this way). Defective dynein: Kartagener syndrome (sinusitis, bronchiectasis, situs inversus, infertility). Colchicine and vincristine act on microtubules.
bc.cell.cyto.why: Dynein carries cargo back towards the cell body, the route rabies virus uses to reach the brain.

bc.heme.syn.note: ALA synthase is rate-limiting (needs B6). Lead blocks ALA dehydratase and ferrochelatase: basophilic stippling, microcytic anaemia. Acute intermittent porphyria (PBG deaminase): belly pain, neuropathy, psychiatric signs, no skin photosensitivity; drugs and fasting trigger attacks. Porphyria cutanea tarda: blisters on sun-exposed skin.
bc.heme.syn.why: ALA synthase is the rate-limiting enzyme of haem synthesis.

bc.heme.bil.note: Haem → biliverdin → unconjugated bilirubin → conjugated in the liver by UDP-glucuronyl transferase. Unconjugated rises: haemolysis, Gilbert (mild, after fasting or stress), Crigler-Najjar, newborn jaundice (immature enzyme). Conjugated rises: Dubin-Johnson (black liver), Rotor, obstruction.
bc.heme.bil.why: Newborns have immature UDP-glucuronyl transferase, so unconjugated bilirubin builds up.

bc.clin.tm.note: AFP: liver cancer and yolk sac tumours. CEA: colorectal. CA-125: ovary. CA 19-9: pancreas. PSA: prostate. β-hCG: choriocarcinoma, molar pregnancy. Calcitonin: medullary thyroid. Used for follow-up rather than screening (PSA aside).
bc.clin.tm.why: AFP is the marker most often raised in hepatocellular carcinoma.

bc.nut.title: Nutrition: protein-energy malnutrition and energy
bc.nut.note: Kwashiorkor: oedema, fatty liver, flaky paint skin, sparse pale hair, low albumin (protein lack). Marasmus: severe wasting without oedema (energy lack). Energy: carbohydrate and protein 4 kcal/g, fat 9 kcal/g, alcohol 7. Essential fatty acids: linoleic and linolenic.
bc.nut.why: Oedema, a swollen belly, sparse discoloured hair and skin depigmentation are kwashiorkor.
